title: Sixth Word Five Degrees Of Profit From Selling The Trust

questions.question: What is the first benefit of giving a person’s life and belongings to Allah?
questions.answer: What does not last in this world becomes lasting in the next life.

questions.question: When a person uses life for Allah’s sake, what does that life produce?
questions.answer: It brings everlasting rewards and blessings.

questions.question: What happens to the moments of life even though they seem to pass away here?
questions.answer: They become beautiful results in the eternal world.

questions.question: What is the second benefit named in the passage?
questions.answer: A person receives Paradise as the great payment.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the third benefit?
questions.answer: A person’s body parts and senses become far more valuable when used for Allah.

questions.question: What example is given first to explain the third benefit?
questions.answer: The mind or intelligence.

questions.question: What happens to a person’s intelligence if it is used only for the nafs?
questions.answer: It becomes harmful and causes pain, worry, and weakness.

questions.question: What two kinds of troubles does misused intelligence bring to a person?
questions.answer: Sadness about the past and fear about the future.

questions.question: Why does the passage say some sinful people run to drinking or pointless fun?
questions.answer: They want to escape the pain caused by their troubled minds.

questions.question: What does intelligence become when it is used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a guide that opens understanding and leads toward eternal happiness.

questions.question: What example is given after intelligence?
questions.answer: The eye.

questions.question: What happens to the eye when it is used for selfish desires?
questions.answer: It falls into a low use by chasing passing beauty and desires.

questions.question: What happens to the eye when it is used in the way Allah allows?
questions.answer: It becomes a means to see Allah’s signs and the wonders in creation.

questions.question: What example is given after the eye?
questions.answer: The tongue and the sense of taste.

questions.question: What happens to the tongue and taste when they are used only for the stomach and the nafs?
questions.answer: They fall to a low job, serving only eating and desire.

questions.question: What do the tongue and taste become when they are used for the Generous Provider?
questions.answer: They become thankful servants that recognize Allah’s mercy in provision.

questions.question: What are readers told to compare with the mind, eye, and tongue?
questions.answer: All the other body parts and abilities.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of nature does a believer gain?
questions.answer: A nature fit for Paradise.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of nature does an unbeliever gain?
questions.answer: A nature fit for Hell.

questions.question: Why does the believer gain a better value?
questions.answer: Because the believer uses Allah’s trust for Allah and within His limits.

questions.question: What does the unbeliever do wrong with the trust?
questions.answer: The unbeliever misuses it for the instinctual self.

questions.question: What is the fourth benefit about human life?
questions.answer: Human beings are weak and needy, so they need to rely on Allah.

questions.question: What happens inside a person who does not trust the All-Powerful One?
questions.answer: The conscience stays troubled and full of pain and regret.

questions.question: What strong image is used for a person who does not rely on Allah?
questions.answer: Such a person may be crushed by suffering or fall to an animal-like state.

questions.question: What is the fifth benefit?
questions.answer: The acts of worship done with one’s body and senses will return as fruits of Paradise at the time of greatest need.

questions.question: Who agrees about this fifth benefit according to the passage?
questions.answer: People of spiritual insight who have seen the truth of things.

questions.question: What change happens to short worldly life when it is given for Allah?
questions.answer: It turns into something everlasting.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about moments that seem to disappear?
questions.answer: They are not wasted if they are used for Allah; they become lasting rewards.

questions.question: In which world do the good results of such moments fully appear?
questions.answer: In the eternal life.

questions.question: What is given as the payment in the second benefit?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: In the third benefit, what happens to human abilities when they are used the right way?
questions.answer: Their worth becomes much greater.

questions.question: Which human ability is discussed first in detail?
questions.answer: Intelligence.

questions.question: If intelligence is used for selfish purposes, how does it affect a person?
questions.answer: It becomes a source of distress and harm.

questions.question: What time periods especially trouble a person when intelligence is misused?
questions.answer: The past and the future.

questions.question: What does this teach about intelligence by itself?
questions.answer: It can help or hurt depending on how it is used.

questions.question: When intelligence is used for Allah, what kind of role does it play?
questions.answer: It helps a person understand creation and move toward eternal joy.

questions.question: What sense is described as a window for the spirit?
questions.answer: The eye.

questions.question: What lowers the eye’s value?
questions.answer: Using it to chase temporary beauty for selfish desire.

questions.question: What raises the eye’s value?
questions.answer: Using it in obedience to Allah and seeing His signs in the world.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the tongue and taste when they are used badly?
questions.answer: They become servants of appetite and bodily desire.

questions.question: What do the tongue and taste become when they are used well?
questions.answer: They become thankful recognizers of Allah’s mercy in food and provision.

questions.question: Why are intelligence, the eye, and the tongue used as examples?
questions.answer: They help explain how all human abilities can be raised or lowered.

questions.question: What should a reader do with the other limbs and senses after hearing these examples?
questions.answer: Compare them in the same way.

questions.question: What does faith help a believer do with Allah’s trust?
questions.answer: Use it for Allah and stay within His limits.

questions.question: What does betrayal of the trust look like in this passage?
questions.answer: Using Allah’s gifts for the selfish nafs instead of for Allah.

questions.question: What kind of person is described in the fourth benefit?
questions.answer: A person who is weak, needy, and surrounded by hardships.

questions.question: What does such a person need to do?
questions.answer: Rely on Allah, trust Him, and submit to Him.

questions.question: What happens if a person refuses that reliance?
questions.answer: The person’s inner life becomes troubled and filled with useless pain.

questions.question: What is the danger of carrying life’s burden without trust in Allah?
questions.answer: It can overwhelm a person and pull him down.

questions.question: What reward is mentioned in the fifth benefit for worship done by one’s body?
questions.answer: It will return as fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: When will that reward be given?
questions.answer: At the moment when a person needs it most.

questions.question: Who confirms this truth in the passage?
questions.answer: Spiritually aware people who have experienced deeper insight.

questions.question: What is the first profit trying to teach about life in this world?
questions.answer: If life is used for Allah, it does not end in loss but continues with lasting reward.

questions.question: How does the passage describe worldly life before it is given for Allah?
questions.answer: It is fading and temporary.

questions.question: What happens to a person’s deeds done for Allah after worldly time passes?
questions.answer: They continue as eternal results.

questions.question: What is the second profit in simple words?
questions.answer: Allah gives Paradise in return.

questions.question: What is special about the third profit compared with the first two?
questions.answer: It explains in detail how different human abilities become more valuable.

questions.question: Which ability is first shown as either helpful or harmful?
questions.answer: The intelligence.

questions.question: What kind of life does misused intelligence create inside a person?
questions.answer: A life full of worry, sorrow, and fear.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about sinful entertainment and drinking?
questions.answer: Some people use them to hide from mental pain.

questions.question: What does rightly used intelligence open up for a person?
questions.answer: Understanding of Allah’s mercy and wisdom in creation.

questions.question: What future does rightly used intelligence prepare a person for?
questions.answer: Eternal happiness.

questions.question: How is the eye described in relation to the spirit?
questions.answer: It is an opening through which the spirit sees the world.

questions.question: What wrong use of the eye is warned against?
questions.answer: Looking after passing beauties in a selfish and desire-driven way.

questions.question: What good use of the eye is praised?
questions.answer: Seeing the signs, art, and mercy of Allah in creation.

questions.question: What body part is connected with the sense of taste?
questions.answer: The tongue.

questions.question: What makes the tongue sink to a low level?
questions.answer: Using it only for appetite and the nafs.

questions.question: What lifts the tongue to a high level?
questions.answer: Using it with gratitude toward the Provider.

questions.question: After these examples, what conclusion are readers supposed to reach about all their other abilities?
questions.answer: The same rule applies to them too.

questions.question: What kind of character does a believer build by using Allah’s trust properly?
questions.answer: A character suitable for Paradise.

questions.question: What kind of character does an unbeliever build by misusing that trust?
questions.answer: A character suitable for Hell.

questions.question: What is the reason given for this difference?
questions.answer: One obeys Allah’s limits, and the other follows the selfish self.

questions.question: What facts about human beings are listed in the fourth profit?
questions.answer: People are helpless, needy, weak, and burdened by life.

questions.question: How can a person face these facts in the right way?
questions.answer: By depending on Allah and trusting Him.

questions.question: What happens to a person who does not do that?
questions.answer: The person is choked by regret, pain, and useless suffering.

questions.question: What is the fifth profit mainly about?
questions.answer: Worship done with one’s body and senses will come back as reward in Paradise.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the “time of greatest need” suggest?
questions.answer: That this reward will help most in the Hereafter, when a person needs it deeply.

questions.question: Who has recognized this truth according to the passage?
questions.answer: Chosen people with spiritual insight and clear witnessing.

questions.question: What does the first profit say happens to temporary possessions and life?
questions.answer: They become everlasting when offered to Allah and used for His sake.

questions.question: Why are the passing moments of life not truly lost for a believer?
questions.answer: Because they turn into lasting blessings and good results.

questions.question: Besides the eternal world, what other stage is mentioned as receiving a bright result from such deeds?
questions.answer: The Intermediate Realm.

questions.question: What is the second profit named in the passage?
questions.answer: Receiving Paradise as the payment.

questions.question: What is increased greatly in the third profit?
questions.answer: The worth of each body part and each sense.

questions.question: What happens when intelligence is controlled by the nafs instead of being used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes harmful and fills a person with heavy worries.

questions.question: What two emotional burdens especially weigh on such a person?
questions.answer: Grief over what is past and fear of what is coming.

questions.question: How does the passage explain some people’s escape into sinful habits?
questions.answer: They try to run from the pain caused by a badly used mind.

questions.question: What does intelligence become when given back to its true Owner?
questions.answer: It becomes a key that opens understanding and guides a person to eternal joy.

questions.question: What makes the eye fall to a lower level?
questions.answer: Using it for selfish looking and temporary attractions.

questions.question: What makes the eye rise to a higher level?
questions.answer: Using it to observe Allah’s signs and beauty within His limits.

questions.question: What poor use of the tongue is criticized?
questions.answer: Using it only for appetite and worldly craving.

questions.question: What noble use of the tongue is praised?
questions.answer: Using taste with thankfulness and awareness of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak directly to the intelligence, eye, and tongue?
questions.answer: To help the reader clearly notice the difference between low use and noble use.

questions.question: What are readers invited to do after these three examples?
questions.answer: Think about the rest of their faculties in the same way.

questions.question: What does the believer’s faith help him do with Allah’s trust?
questions.answer: Use it faithfully for Allah and according to His limits.

questions.question: What does the unbeliever do with that trust?
questions.answer: Misuses it for the selfish desires of the nafs.

questions.question: What kind of result does the believer reach through proper use of Allah’s gifts?
questions.answer: A nature worthy of Paradise.

questions.question: What kind of result does the unbeliever reach through misuse?
questions.answer: A nature fitting for Hell.

questions.question: What does the fourth profit teach about the human condition?
questions.answer: People cannot carry life well on their own because they are weak and needy.

questions.question: What three actions toward Allah are encouraged in the fourth profit?
questions.answer: Relying on Him, trusting Him, and submitting to Him.

questions.question: What happens to the conscience without this reliance?
questions.answer: It stays disturbed and full of pain.

questions.question: What are some results of this inner trouble?
questions.answer: Useless suffering, regrets, and a falling to a lower state.

questions.question: What is promised in the fifth profit for worship done by one’s limbs?
questions.answer: A high reward appearing as fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: When will this reward be especially given?
questions.answer: When the person has the greatest need.

questions.question: What group of people is mentioned as agreeing on this truth?
questions.answer: Spiritually enlightened people who have witnessed reality.

questions.question: In the first profit, what happens to things that normally fade away?
questions.answer: They are changed into something lasting.

questions.question: What condition makes this change happen?
questions.answer: A person must give life and actions for Allah’s sake.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use to show that moments of life are not wasted?
questions.answer: It compares them to seeds that later show beautiful results.

questions.question: What is the reward named in the second profit?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What is the big lesson of the third profit?
questions.answer: Human abilities can either be raised very high or lowered very badly.

questions.question: What is one wrong way to use intelligence?
questions.answer: Using it for selfish desires instead of for Allah.

questions.question: What effect does that wrong use have on a person’s inner life?
questions.answer: It causes heavy sadness and fear.

questions.question: What does the passage say some sinful people do because of this pain?
questions.answer: They turn to drinking or silly amusement.

questions.question: What does intelligence become when it is used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a helpful guide that opens the treasures of meaning in creation.

questions.question: What is one wrong use of the eye?
questions.answer: Looking at temporary beauty in a desire-driven way.

questions.question: What is one right use of the eye?
questions.answer: Seeing Allah’s artistry and signs in the world.

questions.question: What is one wrong use of the tongue and taste?
questions.answer: Serving only hunger and the lower self.

questions.question: What is one right use of the tongue and taste?
questions.answer: Being thankful for Allah’s provision.

questions.question: Why are these three examples important for understanding the passage?
questions.answer: They show how every gift from Allah should be used in the right direction.

questions.question: According to the passage, what gives the believer a Paradise-worthy nature?
questions.answer: Faithful use of Allah’s trust within His boundaries.

questions.question: What gives the unbeliever a Hell-worthy nature?
questions.answer: Betraying the trust by serving the nafs.

questions.question: What does the fourth profit say about human strength?
questions.answer: Human beings are weak and cannot manage everything by themselves.

questions.question: What does the fourth profit say about human needs?
questions.answer: People have many needs and are poor before them.

questions.question: What should a person do because of this weakness and need?
questions.answer: Depend on Allah and trust Him.

questions.question: What happens if a person refuses to rely on Allah?
questions.answer: The person suffers inner distress, regret, and pain.

questions.question: What extreme result can happen to such a person according to the passage?
questions.answer: The person may sink to an animal-like condition.

questions.question: What is the fifth profit about worship?
questions.answer: Worship done by one’s faculties will return as a great reward.

questions.question: What form will that reward take?
questions.answer: It will appear as fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: When will a person receive these fruits?
questions.answer: At the time of greatest need.

questions.question: Who has agreed on this truth?
questions.answer: People who were given spiritual light and insight.

questions.question: What does this whole passage teach about the body and senses?
questions.answer: They are trusts from Allah and should be used in a way that pleases Him.

questions.question: What is the first profit of giving one’s life and property for Allah’s sake?
questions.answer: Temporary life turns into everlasting gain.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to life’s passing moments when they are used for Allah?
questions.answer: They continue as beautiful and blessed results.

questions.question: What is the second profit stated in the passage?
questions.answer: Paradise is given as the price.

questions.question: In the third profit, what happens to the worth of human senses and limbs?
questions.answer: Their worth becomes many times greater.

questions.question: What happens to intelligence when it serves the nafs?
questions.answer: It turns into a harmful burden.

questions.question: What kinds of thoughts trouble a person when intelligence is misused?
questions.answer: Painful memories and fearful expectations.

questions.question: What may a sinful person seek in order to forget this mental pain?
questions.answer: Intoxicants or empty entertainment.

questions.question: What happens to intelligence when it is used on Allah’s behalf?
questions.answer: It becomes a means of unlocking wisdom and mercy in creation.

questions.question: What role does such intelligence play in a person’s future?
questions.answer: It helps prepare the person for eternal happiness.

questions.question: What is the eye able to become if it follows the nafs?
questions.answer: A low tool for selfish desire.

questions.question: What is the eye able to become if it is used for Allah?
questions.answer: A noble observer of Allah’s signs and artistry.

questions.question: What lowers the tongue and taste?
questions.answer: Using them only for appetite and self-centered pleasure.

questions.question: What raises the tongue and taste?
questions.answer: Using them with gratitude toward Allah’s provision.

questions.question: After hearing these examples, what should the reader understand about all the other faculties?
questions.answer: They also rise or fall depending on how they are used.

questions.question: What kind of nature does the believer gain by proper use of these trusts?
questions.answer: A nature suited to Paradise.

questions.question: What kind of nature does the unbeliever gain by improper use?
questions.answer: A nature suited to Hell.

questions.question: What is the reason for this difference between believer and unbeliever?
questions.answer: The believer uses Allah’s trust as Allah wants, while the unbeliever uses it for the nafs.

questions.question: What human weaknesses are named in the fourth profit?
questions.answer: Helplessness, poverty, weakness, and many hardships.

questions.question: What should a person do because of these weaknesses?
questions.answer: Put trust in Allah and submit to Him.

questions.question: What happens to the conscience of someone who does not do this?
questions.answer: It remains troubled.

questions.question: What can these troubles do to a person?
questions.answer: They can overwhelm him with pain and lower his state.

questions.question: What does the fifth profit promise for worship done by one’s members and faculties?
questions.answer: A lofty reward.

questions.question: In what form will that reward come?
questions.answer: As fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: At what time will those fruits be given?
questions.answer: At the time of greatest need.

questions.question: Who is said to agree on this truth?
questions.answer: Those who have spiritual illumination and clear insight into reality.
